dedupe_keys.name: twelve years of united states power outages county day analysis corpus eagle i based

description: This corpus gives county-day power outage burdens for the United States from 2014 to 2025, derived from 249 million 15-minute EAGLE-I outage records audited against the EIA-861 utility census. It was published by Jingle Zhang, Haoran Zhang, Luwen Shen, Boyang Li and Zhao Xu as companion data and code for a study of concentrated extremes and quiet escalation in US outages. It holds a fact table of customer-hours lost per county and day, a layered multi-hazard attribution table (storm events, tropical cyclone tracks, satellite fire, smoke, drought and degree-days), and a county table with repaired customer counts and CDC/ATSDR Social Vulnerability Index vintages, with the full Python pipeline for audits, burden accounting, extremes declustering, restoration survival models, inequality panels and county trend models. Coverage is all US counties by day over twelve years. Files are one ZIP of about 54 MB on Zenodo (version 1.1, September 2026) under CC-BY-4.0 at no cost. Caveats: EAGLE-I coverage of customers varies by utility and year, and hazard attribution is statistical. Simulation uses are outage risk, restoration and equity analysis for grid resilience planning. Related records: none linked on the provider's pages read on the day.
